reviewer_action_required: Reviewer decisions of 2026-09-24 are applied: the operator hints were accepted for the 19 rows where candidate A and candidate B were hinted the same disposition, and ADAPT was chosen for PRP-NFR-019, PRP-NFR-021 and PRP-NFR-022, where candidate A's EV01 hint had left REUSE and ADAPT open. None of these values selects a candidate, because each is the same for A and B; the basis is recorded per row in disposition_basis. PRP-FR-017 and PRP-FR-044 remain UNASSESSED behind stated blockers, as do the 68 rows that no WP24 experiment maps to, which procedure section 8 item 3 allows. Still outstanding for the reviewer: the decision_receipt (candidate selection, rejected_alternatives, rollback_exit_plan and signature) and the seven OPEN deviations.

rows.title: PRP-owned organization isolation

pinned_version.B: vLLM in a Linux container; LiteLLM only as the key/proxy layer in EV03/EV04

observed_capability.A: No organization concept exists: the auth schema has users and API keys only (EV04 step 2).
observed_capability.B: Bare vLLM has no tenancy at all; LiteLLM offers teams (EV04, B).

rows.limitation: A cannot express organization isolation; PRP must own it.
rows.custom_gap: PRP builds organization isolation itself.
rows.maintenance_exit_risk: Adopting the candidate's user model would silently flatten tenancy.
rows.disposition_basis: Reviewer accepted the operator hints on 2026-09-24 (the reviewer is the repository owner, per procedure section 9 item 4). EV04. Candidate A: BUILD-GAP for the key authority, because its store is reversible. Candidate B, bare vLLM: BUILD-GAP for FR-003..009, no scope vocabulary and no revoke API. Both candidates agree, so this value does not select a candidate. Candidate B's LiteLLM layer was hinted CONFIGURE for issuance, scoping, storage and revocation; the operator recorded that whether LiteLLM may be the key authority, against ADR-PRP's rule of exactly one client-key authority, is the reviewer's call and it was NOT taken here.

rows.title: Controlled node enrollment

pinned_version.B: vLLM in a Linux container; LiteLLM only as the key/proxy layer in EV03/EV04

observed_capability.A: The cluster reports its own membership: /v1/workers lists each worker by address with its model replicas, and /v1/supervisor returns the supervisor address (EV02 step 2).
observed_capability.B: vLLM has no enrollment concept; a node is a container someone started (EV02, B).

rows.limitation: Enrollment is implicit: a worker that connects is a member. There is no admission control on nodes.
rows.custom_gap: PRP owns node enrollment and treats the cluster listing as an observation.
rows.maintenance_exit_risk: A rogue local process could register as a worker; nothing authenticates enrollment.

rows.title: Fresh health observations

pinned_version.B: vLLM in a Linux container; LiteLLM only as the key/proxy layer in EV03/EV04

observed_capability.A: Health observations are available but shallow: model presence in /v1/models, worker-to-replica mapping, and a metrics exporter. rows.custom_gap: PRP treats candidate health as a signal only and runs its own liveness probe.

rows.title: Safe runtime lifecycle

source_review.finding: Xinference documents launch/list/terminate and a supervisor/worker topology whose support depends on engine/model combinations; PRP-safe bound routing of a reserved lease to the actual worker is a spike requirement, not a supported-feature claim.

pinned_version.B: vLLM in a Linux container; LiteLLM only as the key/proxy layer in EV03/EV04

observed_capability.A: Lifecycle is safe in the small and unsafe in the large: launch, terminate and relaunch all work, but the supervisor relaunches a dead replica unasked (35-40 s on 0.6B, 131.8 s on the 4B) with a NEW address each time, and killing the supervisor orphans the worker, which keeps the GPU and recreates the model (EV03, EV06, EV07 partial).
observed_capability.B: vLLM does not restart its own engine; the container exits and recovery needs a supervisor (EV06, B).

rows.limitation: Auto-recreation can be bounded by XINFERENCE_MODEL_ACTOR_AUTO_RECOVER_LIMIT but not disabled.
rows.custom_gap: PRP bounds auto-recreate, reconciles after an unrequested relocation, and reaps orphaned workers.
rows.maintenance_exit_risk: An orphaned worker holds VRAM invisibly and resurrects models after a restart.
rows.disposition_basis: Reviewer accepted the operator hints on 2026-09-24 (the reviewer is the repository owner, per procedure section 9 item 4). EV02. Candidate A: ADAPT, and better than B on this gate. Candidate B: ADAPT. Both agree, so the value does not select a candidate.

rows.title: Durable admission transaction

pinned_version.B: vLLM in a Linux container; LiteLLM only as the key/proxy layer in EV03/EV04

observed_capability.A: Candidate side only: the runtime rejects over-limit work with HTTP 429 when request_limits is set, and its in-flight gauge never over-counted (EV05 step 2).
observed_capability.B: vLLM queued the excess instead of rejecting it (EV05, B).

rows.limitation: BLOCKER: the durable admission transaction requires real PostgreSQL and fault injection on the PRP side, which does not exist before M4. The procedure states this explicitly, so AT-017 stays NOT_RUN regardless of candidate behaviour.
rows.custom_gap: PRP implements the durable admission transaction; the candidate contributes only backpressure.
rows.maintenance_exit_risk: Treating a candidate 429 as an admission decision would put the authority in the wrong place.
rows.disposition_basis: Left UNASSESSED on purpose: a BLOCKER is stated in `limitation` and neither candidate hint dispositions it (PRP's own M4 work). Section 8 item 3 accepts a stated blocker.

rows.title: Shared GPU reservation authority

source_review.finding: Ray logical resources are scheduling tokens, not VRAM caps; candidate C must still measure residency and enforce physical admission.

pinned_version.B: vLLM in a Linux container; LiteLLM only as the key/proxy layer in EV03/EV04

observed_capability.A: With request_limits 4, twelve concurrent requests from three processes gave 4x200 and 8x429, and the gauge peaked at exactly 4 with no over-count in 185 scrapes. The default is unlimited (-1), and the rejection is DEFERRED: an over-limit request waited 6.525 s, until the running batch finished, before being refused. The limit is readable only from the unauthenticated metrics exporter, not from /v1/models (EV05). The model also stays resident: 41 idle samples over 20 minutes with no unload, and no idle timeout exists in the code (EV07 partial).
observed_capability.B: max_num_seqs 4 queued the excess in three waves; the value is not exposed by any endpoint (EV05, B).

rows.limitation: EV07's mixed chat/speech load is BLOCKED on WP10, so shared reservation across speech and chat is unmeasured.
rows.custom_gap: PRP sets request_limits explicitly, scrapes the exporter for limit and in-flight, and never relies on the 429 as fast backpressure.
rows.maintenance_exit_risk: The exporter that carries the only readable limit needs no credential.
rows.disposition_basis: Reviewer accepted the operator hints on 2026-09-24 (the reviewer is the repository owner, per procedure section 9 item 4). EV05. Candidate A: CONFIGURE for FR-018, stronger than B on this gate. Candidate B: CONFIGURE for FR-018. Both agree. FR-017 is deliberately left UNASSESSED with a blocker: neither hint dispositions it, because the durable admission transaction is PRP's own M4 work.

rows.title: Uncertain execution fencing

pinned_version.B: vLLM in a Linux container; LiteLLM only as the key/proxy layer in EV03/EV04

observed_capability.A: Fencing is the weak point: killing the engine mid-generation returned HTTP 200 with a truncated stream, no [DONE] and no error object, which is indistinguishable from success by status alone. No blind replay occurred in any case (EV06).
observed_capability.B: An engine kill produced an in-stream error object; a restart produced a stream that stopped with neither (EV06, B).

rows.limitation: Candidate A gives the caller no way to distinguish UNKNOWN from FINISHED at the transport level.
rows.custom_gap: PRP maps any stream ending without an explicit [DONE] to UNKNOWN and never trusts the HTTP status.
rows.maintenance_exit_risk: A client that checks only the status code reads a killed generation as success.
rows.disposition_basis: Reviewer accepted the operator hints on 2026-09-24 (the reviewer is the repository owner, per procedure section 9 item 4). EV06. Candidate A: ADAPT. Candidate B: ADAPT. Both agree.

rows.title: Absolute deadlines and cancellation

pinned_version.B: vLLM in a Linux container; LiteLLM only as the key/proxy layer in EV03/EV04

observed_capability.A: Cancellation works only for streaming: a socket close stopped compute in 3.53 s, but a non-streaming cancel stopped nothing and the model ran 61.5 s longer, producing all 900 tokens. The explicit abort endpoint POST /v1/models/{uid}/requests/{request_id}/abort returned DONE in 2.295 s and left the model idle 0.5 s later (EV06).
observed_capability.B: Client cancel stopped compute within 0.19 s for streaming and non-streaming alike (EV06, B).

rows.limitation: The abort route is absent from the route table and was found only in /openapi.json at runtime; it needs a client-supplied request_id.
rows.custom_gap: PRP generates request_id per attempt and cancels through the abort endpoint, never by closing the socket.
rows.maintenance_exit_risk: Any integration written from the socket-close assumption silently wastes GPU time.
rows.disposition_basis: Reviewer accepted the operator hints on 2026-09-24 (the reviewer is the repository owner, per procedure section 9 item 4). EV06. Candidate A: ADAPT. Candidate B: ADAPT. Both agree.

rows.title: Retry classification

pinned_version.B: vLLM in a Linux container; LiteLLM only as the key/proxy layer in EV03/EV04

observed_capability.A: Retry classification is clean on the candidate side: no request-level retry, failover or hedging exists anywhere in the request path, so there is nothing to disable, and no second attempt was ever made (EV03 step 4, EV06).
observed_capability.B: LiteLLM has retry and fallback that must be configured off (EV03, B).

rows.limitation: The candidate does relocate replicas unasked, which is a different axis from request retry (NFR-023).
rows.custom_gap: PRP classifies retries itself; the candidate adds no hidden attempts to account for.
rows.maintenance_exit_risk: A future version could add request-level retry; the absence is not a configuration guarantee.
rows.disposition_basis: Reviewer accepted the operator hints on 2026-09-24 (the reviewer is the repository owner, per procedure section 9 item 4). EV06. Candidate A: ADAPT. Candidate B: ADAPT. Both agree.

source_review.finding: vLLM provides OpenAI-compatible serving; the PRP client subset must be tested against the pinned release because endpoint and security behaviour depend on the release.

Xinference documents launch/list/terminate and a supervisor/worker topology whose support depends on engine/model combinations; PRP-safe bound routing of a reserved lease to the actual worker is a spike requirement, not a supported-feature claim.
Ray Serve LLM is conditional candidate C for replica orchestration, not an automatic requirement and not stacked on Xinference by default.
FastAPI/Pydantic are the first evaluation candidate for typed request validation and OpenAPI on the thin API; API processes never load models.

rows.title: API and model process isolation
rows.srs_section: 6.1 Python-first และ framework reuse constraints

source_review.finding: FastAPI worker processes have separate memory; model globals must not live in web workers and adding workers must not multiply resident models.
vLLM engine/native process behaviour and start-method constraints are version-sensitive; verify against the selected release and keep the engine in its own environment.

pinned_version.B: vLLM in a Linux container; LiteLLM only as the key/proxy layer in EV03/EV04

observed_capability.A: Process isolation holds by construction: the API process, the worker and one sub-pool per model replica are separate processes, confirmed repeatedly (EV05 step 1, EV06, EV07 partial).
observed_capability.B: vLLM runs the engine in its own process inside the container (EV01/EV06, B).

rows.limitation: Isolation also means the API listener is not the whole system: killing it leaves the worker alive.
rows.custom_gap: PRP manages the process tree, not a single process.

source_review.finding: Xinference documents launch/list/terminate and a supervisor/worker topology whose support depends on engine/model combinations; PRP-safe bound routing of a reserved lease to the actual worker is a spike requirement, not a supported-feature claim.

LiteLLM virtual keys/routing are an optional key or router layer for A or B, not a mandatory dependency and not a reason for a second user-key store; implicit retries, failover or hedging must not bypass admission or the original deadline.
Ray logical resources are scheduling tokens, not VRAM caps; candidate C must still measure residency and enforce physical admission.

pinned_version.B: vLLM in a Linux container; LiteLLM only as the key/proxy layer in EV03/EV04

observed_capability.A: Binding to a model UID held for 40 of 40 requests, and there is no request-level retry or hedging to disable. But the client cannot choose or even see a replica (strict 0,1,0,1 round-robin, no replica named in any response), and the supervisor RELOCATES replicas unasked with a new address each time, which is what the requirement forbids (EV03).
observed_capability.B: LiteLLM's retry and fallback had to be configured off; binding held once they were (EV03, B).

rows.limitation: One GPU host, so this is replica binding rather than host binding (DEV-03).
rows.custom_gap: PRP runs one replica per UID, bounds auto-recreate, reconciles after relocation, and scrapes the exporter for per-replica attribution.
rows.maintenance_exit_risk: An address PRP recorded stops being valid after any unrequested recovery.
